article.headline: SK Hynix's AI Memory Grip Spans Every Time Zone
article.lede: A South Korean chipmaker provides the memory inside virtually every major AI accelerator now running, and since early 2025 has led the world in DRAM revenue. Its commercial footprint spans fourteen countries, and its profit margins rival those of software businesses.
article.body:
The phrase borrows the old British Empire epithet and applies it to **SK Hynix** (000660.KS), a semiconductor company headquartered in Icheon, South Korea, and since early 2025 the world's leading *DRAM* maker by revenue. Across fourteen countries it operates seventy-eight subsidiaries — regional *trading entities* named Hynix America, Hynix UK, Hynix Deutschland, Hynix Japan, and so on — each acting as a local importer and seller of memory chips. Their collective timezone span means a sales office is always open; the structure deliberately echoes the colonial trading house.

What gives the metaphor its present bite is *HBM*, or **High Bandwidth Memory** — stacked *DRAM* chips mounted atop AI accelerators to ferry data at speeds conventional memory cannot match. SK Hynix holds roughly 70 to 80 percent of the market for *HBM3E*, the generation inside every NVIDIA (NVDA) H100 and H200 GPU now in service; through 2025, roughly ninety percent of NVIDIA's HBM supply came from SK Hynix alone. For the successor generation, *HBM4*, the company has reportedly secured about two-thirds of NVIDIA's allocation, with Samsung (005930.KS) and Micron Technology (MU) competing for the remainder.

The commercial consequence is exceptional. In fiscal year 2025 the company posted revenue of roughly ₩97 trillion (about $68 billion), an operating margin of 49 percent, and net income of ₩42.9 trillion — more than double the prior year. Its market capitalization approached $950 billion in May 2026, placing it among the twenty most valuable companies on Earth and within reach of the trillion-dollar threshold. The surge reflects a strategic bet: converting more capacity to high-margin HBM than rivals did, which allowed it to displace Samsung (005930.KS) as the world's top *DRAM* maker by revenue for the first time in the company's forty-year history.

The empire is also acquiring new territory. In March 2025, SK Hynix (000660.KS) broke ground on a $3.87 billion *advanced-packaging* facility in West Lafayette, Indiana — its first manufacturing site on American soil — backed by $458 million in US *CHIPS Act* subsidies. The plant, targeted for completion in 2028, will produce the *2.5D packaging* stacks that bond HBM dies to AI processors. A simultaneous organizational restructure created a dedicated HBM technical unit in the Americas, stationed near the hyperscale customers — NVIDIA (NVDA), Google (GOOGL), Microsoft (MSFT), Amazon (AMZN) — whose appetite for memory the company now defines.

concepts.definition: A type of DRAM in which multiple memory chips are stacked vertically and connected by thousands of short wires through the chip body (through-silicon vias). Stacking allows far wider data buses than conventional memory, delivering bandwidth of a terabyte or more per second — essential for AI training and inference workloads.

Dynamic Random-Access Memory, the dominant form of volatile main memory used in computers and servers. Each memory cell stores a charge that must be refreshed thousands of times per second. SK Hynix, Samsung Electronics, and Micron Technology together control roughly 95 percent of global DRAM production.

The third generation of High Bandwidth Memory, Extended — the E suffix denotes a capacity and speed upgrade over the base HBM3 specification. HBM3E stacks reach 36 gigabytes per stack with bandwidth exceeding 1.2 terabytes per second. It is the memory type inside NVIDIA's H100 and H200 GPUs.

The fourth-generation High Bandwidth Memory standard, entering mass production in 2026. HBM4 targets higher per-stack capacity and bandwidth, and introduces a wider interface to the connected processor die. SK Hynix is the leading supplier for NVIDIA's next-generation GPU platforms using HBM4.

Semiconductor manufacturing techniques that integrate multiple chips into a single module — by stacking them vertically, placing them side by side on a dense substrate, or combining both approaches. Advanced packaging allows chipmakers to combine memory and logic at very short distances without designing each function on a single die.

An advanced packaging method in which chips are placed side by side on a dense silicon interposer and connected by very short wires. The 2.5D label distinguishes it from full 3D stacking (chips on top of each other) while offering much shorter interconnects than conventional board-level assembly. This approach is used to combine HBM stacks with AI processor dies in products like NVIDIA's H100.

The Creating Helpful Incentives to Produce Semiconductors and Science Act, signed into US law in August 2022. It appropriates approximately $52 billion for domestic semiconductor manufacturing subsidies, with the explicit goal of rebuilding US chip production capacity and reducing supply-chain dependence on East Asia.

In the structure of Korean and Japanese industrial groups, a trading entity (or trading subsidiary) is a legally separate company that imports, distributes, and sells the parent's products in a specific territory. It manages local pricing, customs, and customer relationships, acting as the commercial face of the manufacturer in that market.

ticker_000660-ks.name: SK hynix Inc.
ticker_000660-ks.blurb: SK hynix Inc. researches, develops, manufactures, and sells semiconductor devices, including DRAM, NAND flash, SSD, MCP, and CMM products. The company serves server, networking, mobile, PC, consumer, and automotive markets. It is one of the world's largest memory chipmakers, competing directly with Samsung Electronics and Micron Technology.
ticker_000660-ks.recent: In the past 30 days, SK hynix reported earnings on April 23, 2026, with revenue and net income surging on a memory price upcycle. The stock hit a 52-week high of 1,653,000 KRW, reflecting strong demand for AI-related memory chips. Morningstar raised its fair value estimate by 65% following the earnings report.

ticker_nvda.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ticker_nvda.blurb: NVIDIA designs graphics processing units (GPUs) and system-on-chip products. Originally a gaming chip company, it became the dominant supplier of AI accelerators — chips that perform the parallel matrix math required to train and run large language models. Its H100, H200, and Blackwell GPU families are the de facto standard for AI training infrastructure at hyperscalers and cloud providers. NVIDIA's CUDA software ecosystem creates deep switching costs: virtually all AI frameworks and models are optimised for CUDA, making competing hardware difficult to adopt at scale. NVIDIA also sells networking (InfiniBand, Ethernet) and data-centre systems.
ticker_nvda.recent: NVIDIA reported FY2026 (ending Jan 2026) revenue of $215.9 billion, up 65% YoY, with data centre revenue reaching $186 billion. The company's forward P/E of ~17.5x on 34.8% projected EPS growth produces a PEG of 0.50 — unusually cheap for what is arguably the most critical infrastructure company in the AI buildout. Hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta) collectively committed over $200 billion in AI infrastructure capex for 2026, the majority flowing through NVIDIA's supply chain.

ticker_005930-ks.name: Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd.
ticker_005930-ks.blurb: Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd. is a South Korean multinational electronics company and the world's largest manufacturer of memory chips, smartphones, and consumer electronics. It operates through four divisions: Device eXperience (DX), Device Solutions (DS), SDC, and Harman, covering products from smartphones and TVs to semiconductors and home appliances. As of 2026, it holds a dominant market position in memory and mobile devices, with a market cap exceeding 1,700 trillion KRW.
ticker_005930-ks.recent: In the past 30 days, Samsung Electronics reported strong quarterly earnings driven by blistering memory price hikes, leading to a 46% increase in fair value estimates. The stock hit a 52-week high of 277,000 KRW, reflecting a 390% year-over-year gain. Analysts have raised price targets amid robust demand for AI-related memory chips.

ticker_mu.name: Micron Technology, Inc.
ticker_mu.blurb: Micron is the only US-headquartered manufacturer of DRAM and NAND memory at scale, competing with Samsung and SK Hynix. Historically the most cyclical of the three, it has spent the past two years repositioning toward high-bandwidth memory (HBM), the stacked DRAM that pairs with AI accelerators, where pricing is multiples of standard DDR5 and contracts are multi-year rather than spot.
ticker_mu.recent: In March 2026 Micron began mass production of HBM4 12-Hi 36GB stacks for Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform; management has stated 2026 HBM capacity is sold out under binding agreements. Fiscal Q2 2026 revenue was around $23.9 billion, with non-GAAP gross margin near 75%. The board approved a 30% dividend increase and roughly $25 billion of fiscal-2026 capex. Despite a strong year-to-date move, the forward P/E remains in the high single digits on consensus, reflecting residual cyclicality scepticism.

ticker_googl.name: Alphabet Inc. (Class A)
ticker_googl.blurb: Alphabet is the parent company of Google, the world's dominant search engine, as well as YouTube, the Google Cloud Platform, and a portfolio of moonshot bets (Waymo, DeepMind, Verily). Search advertising accounts for the majority of revenue, but the cloud division has grown into a multi-billion-dollar profit centre. Alphabet is also a leading player in generative AI, having developed the Gemini family of large language models and integrated them across its product suite.
ticker_googl.recent: Alphabet reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $370 billion, with Google Cloud crossing $50 billion annually. The company has faced antitrust scrutiny in both the US and EU, with a US federal court ruling in 2024 that Google holds an illegal monopoly in general search. Despite regulatory headwinds, the stock has benefited from AI-driven search enhancements and strong cloud growth. Paul Pelosi exercised call options with a $150 strike (purchased January 2025, exercised January 2026) gaining approximately 75% over the period.

ticker_msft.name: Microsoft Corporation
ticker_msft.description: Microsoft is a global software, cloud, and AI platform company. Its principal segments are Productivity and Business Processes (Office, LinkedIn, Dynamics), Intelligent Cloud (Azure, server products), and More Personal Computing (Windows, Xbox, Surface). The company is in a structural transition from a capital-light software licensor to a capital-intensive hyperscale cloud and AI infrastructure provider.
ticker_msft.blurb: Microsoft is a global software, cloud, and AI platform company. Its principal segments are Productivity and Business Processes (Office, LinkedIn, Dynamics), Intelligent Cloud (Azure, server products), and More Personal Computing (Windows, Xbox, Surface). The company is in a structural transition from a capital-light software licensor to a capital-intensive hyperscale cloud and AI infrastructure provider.
ticker_msft.recent: As of early May 2026, MSFT trades near $413 — down approximately 25.6% from its July 31, 2025 all-time high of $555.45 and -15.7% YTD — after touching a March 28 correction low of $356.07. The drawdown carried the stock briefly below its 200-week moving average for the first time in roughly 13 years (prior touches: 2009, 2018, 2020, 2022). Revenue grew 18% YoY with Azure +40%, while annualized AI revenue reached approximately $37 billion; calendar-2026 capex is projected near $190 billion and free cash flow contracted -22% YoY. Forward P/E is approximately 24.4.

ticker_amzn.name: Amazon.com, Inc.
ticker_amzn.blurb: Amazon operates the world's largest e-commerce marketplace and the leading cloud infrastructure platform, Amazon Web Services (AWS). AWS generates the majority of Amazon's operating profit despite representing a minority of total revenue. The company also has significant positions in digital advertising, streaming (Prime Video), and logistics infrastructure. Amazon is a major investor in AI, both through AWS cloud AI services and through a multi-billion-dollar strategic stake in Anthropic.
ticker_amzn.recent: Amazon reported FY2025 revenue exceeding $650 billion, with AWS growing at roughly 17% annually and crossing $100 billion in run-rate revenue. The advertising segment has become a meaningful profit contributor. Paul Pelosi exercised call options with a $150 strike (purchased January 2025, exercised January 2026), with the stock gaining approximately 10% over that period — the weakest performer in the Pelosi 2026 exercise batch.
